who: Laozi · Tao Te Ching 64, tr. James Legge, 1891
quote: The tree which fills the arms grew from the tiniest sprout; ... the journey of a thousand li commenced with a single step.
meaning: A huge tree began as a tiny sprout. A very long trip begins with one step. Every big thing starts small.

who: Hesiod · Works and Days, tr. Hugh G. Evelyn-White, 1914
quote: ...if you add only a little to a little and do this often, soon that little will become great.
meaning: Put a little on a little, again and again, and it grows big. Hesiod was a Greek farmer-poet who lived about 2,700 years ago.

quote: When you derive pleasure and pride in perfecting seemingly "minor" details... big things eventually start falling into place.
meaning: This basketball coach won 10 US college titles. At his first team meeting, he showed his players how to put on their socks, so they would not get blisters.

who: Xunzi · An Encouragement to Study, tr. Homer H. Dubs, 1928
quote: ...unless a person adds steps and half-steps to each other, he cannot go a thousand li; unless little streams are gathered, rivers and seas cannot be formed.
meaning: No long road without many small steps. No sea without many small streams. A li is about half a kilometre.

who: The Buddha · Samyutta Nikaya 22.101, tr. Bhikkhu Sujato
quote: They don't know how much of the handle was worn away today, how much yesterday... They just know what has been worn away.
meaning: A builder never sees his tool handle wear down in one day, but the marks of his fingers end up in the wood. Daily practice changes you the same way.

who: Confucius · Analects IX, tr. James Legge
quote: Though but one basketful is thrown at a time, the advancing with it is my own going forward.
meaning: Build a hill one basket of earth at a time. Each basket moves you forward, and if you stop, only you stopped you.

who: Ninomiya Sontoku · in R. C. Armstrong, Just Before the Dawn, 1912
quote: Great things are the result of an accumulation of little things. ... When you cultivate many acres of land, you do so spadeful by spadeful.
meaning: A big field is dug one spadeful at a time. As a poor orphan boy in Japan, Ninomiya planted rice seedlings that farmers had thrown away, and grew his first bag of rice.

who: Pliny the Elder on the painter Apelles · Natural History 35.84, 1855 translation
quote: ...never to let any day pass, however busy he might be, without exercising himself by tracing some outline or other...
meaning: Apelles, the most famous painter of ancient Greece, drew at least one line every day, even on busy days. The saying 'no day without a line' comes from him.

quote: A small daily task, if it be really daily, will beat the labours of a spasmodic Hercules. It is the tortoise which always catches the hare.
meaning: A small job done every day beats a huge effort done now and then. For years, Trollope wrote every morning from 5:30, before breakfast.

who: The Buddha · Dhammapada 239, tr. E. W. Burlingame, 1921
quote: One after another, little by little, time after time, a wise man should blow away his own impurities, even as a smith blows away the impurities of silver.
meaning: A silversmith cleans silver a tiny bit at a time, until it shines. A wise person cleans their own habits the same way.
